name: Hammer Power Diesel (Black Night)
bestFor: League bowlers who want a dial fit and swappable soles.
myTake: I like the interchangeable soles and love the dial fit. They're easy to put on and take off. I asked the pro shop where I bought them what happens if the plastic laces break, and he said they won't; I haven't had any issues. I rarely change the sole, but I'd get a backup sole and break it in, so if something happens to the one you're using (like stepping in water) you can swap to one that feels exactly the same.

reviewerNotes.note: Their testers found the shoes comfortable and durable, and said the BOA dial held up in extended use despite early doubts about its durability.
The retailer's answer says the BOA lacing system comes with a lifetime guarantee for repairs or replacements.
A few buyers praise the true-to-size fit, the BOA dial, and the interchangeable slide soles.

name: Dexter Pro Am II
soles: Classic rubber outsole with a slide sole on the slide foot

reviewerNotes.note: Buyers call it a comfortable, well-made step up from universal shoes and good value under $100. A few report stitching coming apart.
Reviewers praise the comfort and its value for beginners. One says the laces loosen during a three-game set.
Buyers disagree on slide. Several say the shoes grip instead of sliding, and the retailer confirms the soles can't be swapped.
One buyer found them lightweight and comfortable with a good fit.
A first-time buyer had no complaints.
Another buyer found it comfortable with accurate sizing but reported black marks on the lane when dragging the sole.
